translationRepairs: He also asked that four hundred musket infantry be added to the garrison at Huining city.
He also asked that four hundred musket infantry be added to the garrison at Huiyuan city.
Chinese 惠遠城 is Huiyuan; Huining would render 惠寧, a different Ili city.
He also memorialized to add four hundred musket infantry at Huining city.
He also memorialized to add four hundred musket infantry at Huiyuan city.
Literal likewise misreads 惠遠城 as Huining; Huiyuan is required.
Huining city was more than thirty years old and its population was growing steadily; he extended the walls on the east side, adding a quarter to the area of the old city.
Huiyuan city was more than thirty years old and its population was growing steadily; he extended the walls on the east side, adding a quarter to the area of the old city.
Focus unit again names 惠遠城, so idiomatic Huining is the wrong city.
Huining city had been founded more than thirty years; as the population grew daily, he extended construction east of the city, enlarging the old city by one quarter.
Huiyuan city had been founded more than thirty years; as the population grew daily, he extended construction east of the city, enlarging the old city by one quarter.
Literal must render 惠遠城 as Huiyuan, not Huining.

In the eighth year, because a joint memorial on the empress dowager Xiaoshu's tomb rites used improper wording, his titles were stripped and his rank reduced by one degree, but he was retained in office.
In the eighth year, because a joint memorial on Empress Xiaoshu's tomb rites used improper wording, his titles were stripped and his rank reduced by one degree, but he was retained in office.
孝淑皇后 is Empress Xiaoshu; the Chinese has no 太后 and does not call her empress dowager.
In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he was singled out for rapid promotion to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and made vice commander of a Banner as well.
In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he was singled out for rapid promotion to academician of the Grand Secretariat and made vice commander of a Banner as well.
內閣學士 is academician of the Grand Secretariat, not 文華殿大學士 (Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory).
In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he was promoted by special selection to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, concurrently vice commander of the Banner.
In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong he was promoted by special selection to Academician of the Grand Secretariat, concurrently vice commander of the Banner.
Literal likewise conflates 內閣學士 with the Hall of Literary Glory grand secretaryship.
Vice Commander Han Jiaye urged him strongly: "If they refuse to listen and the governor-general is killed, the nation's prestige will suffer greatly and the court will be mocked throughout the realm.
Vice Commander Han Jiaye urged him strongly: "If they refuse to listen and the governor-general is killed, the nation's prestige will suffer greatly and the empire will become a laughingstock.
為天下笑 means becoming a laughingstock of the realm; idiomatic invents 'the court' as the mocked subject.
The Jiaqing emperor greatly approved and accepted this.
Emperor Renzong greatly approved and accepted this.
Chinese 仁宗 is the temple name Renzong; the literal field should keep that form rather than the idiomatic reign title Jiaqing.

Huining city needed eighty thousand mu and Huining's companion settlement forty thousand; he diverted water from north of the Ili River into canals winding for dozens of li, and also brought spring water in from the northwest of the city.

Huiyuan city needed eighty thousand mu and Huining city forty thousand; he diverted water from north of the Ili River into canals winding for dozens of li, and also brought spring water in from the northwest of the city.
惠遠城 and 惠寧城 are two distinct cities; repeating Huining and inventing a companion settlement misnames both.

Huining city required 80,000 mu and Huining's companion city 40,000 mu; he therefore diverted water north of the Ili River to open canals winding for several tens of li, and also channeled springs northwest of the city.

Huiyuan city required 80,000 mu and Huining city 40,000 mu; he therefore diverted water north of the Ili River to open canals winding for several tens of li, and also channeled springs northwest of the city.
Literal likewise mislabels 惠遠 as Huining and collapses 惠寧 into a companion city.
Together with Grand Canal Director Wu Jin he surveyed the estuary and asked that the old channel be restored.
Together with Grand Canal Director Wu Jing he surveyed the estuary and asked that the old channel be restored.
吳璥 is Wu Jing; Jin is a wrong reading of 璥.
Together with Grand Canal Director Wu Jin he inspected the estuary and requested restoration of the old channel.
Together with Grand Canal Director Wu Jing he inspected the estuary and requested restoration of the old channel.
Literal repeats the same mistransliteration of 吳璥 as Wu Jin.
He also charged that at Huangnizui and Yujiatan Wu Jin had cut channels straight across bends, causing stagnation and siltation—a charge that Jin and others disputed.
He also charged that at Huangnizui and Yujiatan Wu Jing had cut channels straight across bends, causing stagnation and siltation—a charge that Jing and others disputed.
Full and shortened forms 吳璥/璥 must be Jing, not Jin.
He also charged that Wu Jin, at Huangnizui and Yujiatan, had cut straight across bends and thereby caused stagnation and siltation, which Jin and others rebutted in debate.
He also charged that Wu Jing, at Huangnizui and Yujiatan, had cut straight across bends and thereby caused stagnation and siltation, which Jing and others rebutted in debate.
Literal likewise mistransliterates 吳璥 and 璥 as Jin.

He also reported in secret that Wu Jin and Xu Duan's claims were false and that engineering figures had been fabricated, asked to be transferred to grand canal director to investigate the abuses, and recommended Jiang Youqian and Sun Yuting as capable appointees.

He also reported in secret that Wu Jing and Xu Duan's claims were false and that engineering figures had been fabricated, asked to be transferred to grand canal director to investigate the abuses, and recommended Jiang Youqian and Sun Yuting as capable appointees.
吳璥 in the secret memorial must be Wu Jing, not Wu Jin.

He also secretly reported that the arguments of Wu Jin and Xu Duan were untrue and that engineering figures were fabricated, requested transfer to the post of Grand Canal Director to investigate the abuses, and recommended Jiang Youqian and Sun Yuting as capable men.

He also secretly reported that the arguments of Wu Jing and Xu Duan were untrue and that engineering figures were fabricated, requested transfer to the post of Grand Canal Director to investigate the abuses, and recommended Jiang Youqian and Sun Yuting as capable men.
Literal mistransliterates 吳璥 as Wu Jin.
Yar Muhammad wanted him honored as khan, sent envoys asking permission to appoint his own khoja begs, and to tax Andijan merchants under Kokand's tariff rules.
Yar Muhammad wanted him honored as khan, sent envoys asking permission to appoint his own qazi begs, and to tax Andijan merchants under Kokand's tariff rules.
哈子伯克 is qazi beg; khoja would be 和卓, which the Chinese does not use here.
Yar Muhammad wished to have him honored as khan, sent envoys requesting permission to appoint his own khoja begs, and to levy taxes on Andijan merchants by Kokand's tax rules.
Yar Muhammad wished to have him honored as khan, sent envoys requesting permission to appoint his own qazi begs, and to levy taxes on Andijan merchants by Kokand's tax rules.
Literal likewise mistranslates 哈子伯克 as khoja begs.
On further charges he was demoted step by step to commandant of the Vanguard.
On further charges he was demoted step by step to cavalry commandant.
驍騎校 is a Banner cavalry officer rank, not a Vanguard (前鋒) commandant.
On further charges he was demoted in succession to commandant of the Vanguard.
On further charges he was demoted in succession to cavalry commandant.
Literal makes the same office error for 驍騎校.

That autumn the Jiaqing emperor died at Rehe; as the coffin returned to the capital, the future Daoguang emperor walked among the officials, saw Song Yun, supported him and wept; the next day Song Yun was made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and then Left Censor-in-Chief.

That autumn the Jiaqing emperor died at Rehe; as the coffin returned to the capital, the Daoguang emperor walked among the officials, saw Song Yun, supported him and wept; the next day Song Yun was made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and then Left Censor-in-Chief.
After 仁宗崩 the text names 宣宗; 'future' wrongly implies he was not yet the reigning emperor.
He rose in stages to Mongol Reader of the Grand Secretariat, grand secretary academician, and vice banner commander as well.
He rose in stages to Mongol Reader of the Grand Secretariat, Grand Secretariat academician, and vice banner commander as well.
內閣學士 is Grand Secretariat academician; 'grand secretary academician' confuses it with 大學士.
The following year, in the capital evaluation, for proclaiming merit at Jilin he was granted consideration for promotion.
The following year, in the capital evaluation, for his labors at Jilin he was granted consideration for promotion.
宣勞 means laboring/exerting oneself in service, not proclaiming merit.
yet constrained by circumstances, results did not fully match what was planned—how arduous was the founding of the dynasty!
yet constrained by circumstances, results did not fully match what was planned—how arduous was the work of founding and building!
In this colonization coda, 締造之艱 is the difficulty of founding and building the frontier enterprise, not the founding of the Qing dynasty.
